source: AI Agent Orchestration 2026 — Symphony Solutions / JetBrains / Firecrawl landscape survey
summary: 2026 landscape overview: shift from conversational to operational agents, hierarchical multi-agent orchestration, federated orchestration via MCP, shared memory fabric patterns. No specific new technique — general market direction coverage.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — covers patterns AgentForge's architecture already embodies (explicit state machine, sequential determinism). No actionable gap surfaced.

source: Andrej Karpathy — AutoResearch & Karpathy Loop (NextBigFuture / MindStudio coverage)
summary: Karpathy's AutoResearch closes the full research loop: design experiments, edit code, collect data, optimize—700 experiments in 2 days on one GPU. The 'Karpathy Loop' refers to recursive agentic loops for coding agents with state on disk.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — confirms AgentForge's architecture direction (CLI agents, disk artifacts, explicit state). Autonomous experiment loops are out-of-scope for orchestration platform. Self-improving loop concept overlaps with distillation (already shipped).

source: Self-Improving AI Agents Reflection Loop — Taskade / AnalyticsVidhya / Arize survey
summary: Three-layer self-improvement loop (reflection, memory, optimization) for coding agents. Key 2026 finding: self-improvement only reliable in objectively verifiable domains (code compiles or not). Telemetry + critique grounded in process reward models.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — reflection/memory layers map to distillation (shipped). The telemetry angle aligns with HID-163 (already tracked). Nothing novel beyond tracked issues.

source: LangGraph Q2 2026 releases — per-node timeouts, error handlers, DeltaChannel, v2 streaming
summary: LangGraph v0.4 (April 2026) added per-node TimeoutPolicy (run_timeout/idle_timeout), typed NodeError handlers with Saga/compensation routing, DeltaChannel for incremental checkpointing, and a v2 unified StreamPart streaming API.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses its own state machine rather than LangGraph. Timeout patterns are partially relevant to HID-167 (automatic retry). Nothing that isn't already tracked.

source: Agent Memory 2026 — Mem0 benchmark report / Zylos / MAGMA architecture
summary: 2026 memory taxonomy settled: episodic, semantic, procedural. MAGMA (Multi-Graph based Agentic Memory Architecture) leads LoCoMo benchmark at 0.7 score. Token-efficient single-pass hierarchical extraction released April 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — skill distillation (shipped) + HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory) cover this theme. No new gap opened by MAGMA for AgentForge's architecture.

source: Microsoft AutoGen — maintenance mode, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA April 2026
summary: AutoGen entered maintenance mode October 2025. Microsoft Agent Framework (merging AutoGen + Semantic Kernel) reached GA April 2026. No new orchestration innovations — this is consolidation/deprecation news.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — out of scope; AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents, not AutoGen-style framework abstractions.

source: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents (arXiv 2605.06614, May 2026)
summary: SkillOS decouples a frozen executor from a trainable skill curator that updates an external SkillRepo from accumulated experience. Composite RL rewards train the curator on grouped task streams; earlier trajectories update the repo, later related tasks evaluate updates. Skills evolve into richer meta-skills in Markdown. Outperforms memory-free and memory baselines across multi-turn and single-turn tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to AgentForge's verified gap: executor prompts don't receive distilled skills (planner does, executor doesn't). SkillOS demonstrates the curator/executor decoupling pattern that AgentForge could adopt without retraining. The RL training component is out of scope, but the static skill retrieval + injection into executor prompts is directly implementable on top of agentSkillRepository.ts and executorAgent.ts. BLOCKED this run: backlog at 10-issue cap.

source: Skill Retrieval Augmentation (SRA) — arXiv 2604.24594; SkillsInjector — arXiv 2605.29794
summary: SRA: new paradigm for dynamically retrieving and injecting skills from a large out-of-context collection at inference time. SkillsInjector: renderer adapts skill context at injection time, conditioning each description on co-injected skills. Both address cold-start skill selection for frozen executors.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — same theme as SkillOS. Executor skill injection gap in AgentForge is confirmed (verified in executorAgent.ts vs plannerAgent.ts grep). Cannot act this run due to backlog cap. Tag for next run.
